Dilshadbanu W/O Mohamedshafi ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai
Nanavati on 10 December, 2024
 
 C/Fa/787/2013 Order

DA  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 787 of 2013  ==========================================================
 DILSHADBANU W/O MOHAMEDSHAFI IBRAHIMBHAI MEMON  Versus  SURESHBHAI LALBHAI NANAVATI & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR MTM HAKIM(1190) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  MS KIRTI S PATHAK(9966) for the Defendant(s) No. 2  NOTICE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 10/12/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The instant appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 challenges the judgment and award dated 10.01.2013 passed in M.A.C.P. No.411 of 2011 by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Sabarkantha at Himatnagar.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Sabarkantha at Himatnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are as under.

2.1 On 24.04.2011, applicant along with her two children were standing on eastern side of road from Ilol Cross road, at that time, at about 5.15 pm, driver of Car No.GJ-9-AG-7191 came driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed applicant and minor Soban, applicant of MACP No.412 of 2011 and as a result of which, the claimants received injuries.
Therefore, claimants filed claim petition for compensation.
2.2 FIR of incident was registered before the concerned Police Station.
Dilshadbanu W/O Mohamedshafi ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai Nanavati on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104320257/

1  
 C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED: 1  
2.3.
The claimant filed claim petition under section 166 of MV Act being MACP No.411 of 2011 claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- along with interest jointly and severally from the opponents.
2.4. After appreciating evidence on record, learned Tribunal was pleased to pass judgment and award in tune of Rs.2,90,505/- with 8% interest from the date of claim petition.
2.5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with impugned judgment and award dated 10.01.2013, the original claimant has filed present appeal.
3. Learned advocate for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal committed error in taking income of the claimant.
At the relevant time, she was 32 years and she was engaged in stitching work and she was home maker.
It is submitted that looking to this aspect, learned Tribunal ought to have considered rate of minimum wages to calculate loss of future prospects.
It is also submitted that claimant has undergone surgery and sustains two fracture.
It is submitted that considering this aspect, compensation under pain, shock and suffering may also be enhanced.
Therefore, it is submitted to allow the appeal.
4. On the other hand, learned advocate for the Insurance Company supports the judgment and award delivered by the learned Tribunal.
It is submitted that claimant has suffered disability on lower limb side.
According to medical certificate produced, the claimant has suffered 42% disability on lower limb and 33% disability on upper limb.
It is submitted that learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined Tribunal has assessed 28% functional disability.
It is submitted that looking to the percentage of disability on lower side, the Court may not grant compensation for future prospects.
So far as earning of claimant is concerned, there is no evidence produced on record that same is reduced subsequent to injury received from road accident.
Therefore, it is submitted to pass necessary orders.

Dilshadbanu W/O Mohamedshafi ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai Nanavati on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104320257/
2 5.
Apt to note that the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of Legislation.
The concept of just and fair compensation is integral and seminal to the MV Act.

The compensation to be awarded under the principle of just and fair compensation to the injured of the road accident or the legal representative/s of the deceased person is based on the principle of fairness, reasonableness and equability.

Anguish of the heart or for mental turbulence being consequential result of the road accident cannot be actually compensated, but the quint essentiality lies in adopting holistic and pragmatic view to the computation of the compensation for the loss sustained, which is to be in the realm of realistic approximation.
Although exact or perfect arithmetical calculation of compensation for reparation of the loss arrived from the road accident is almost impossible.
The Tribunal is bestowed with duty to make an endevour to award just compensation regardless of the amount claimed by the claimants.
The determination of the quantum of compensation therefore, must be liberal and not niggardly since the law values life and limb in a free country in generous scale.

Needless to state that money may be awarded, so that something tangible may be procured to reach something else of the like nature, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED:
10/12/2024 undefined which has been destroyed or lost, but money cannot renew physical frame that has been battered and shattered being a result of the road accident.

Yet Tribunal to endavour to bring back victim to stage of pre-road accident as far as possible Thus, the award must be reasonable and cannot be assessed with moderation though it cannot at the same time be pity and what could be granted must be just, fair and equitable compensation.
6.

Having heard learned advocates for both sides, and perusing Record and Proceedings, at the outset, it is to be noted that main plank of argument of learned advocate Ms.Pathak for Insurance Company is that claimant having suffered 20% functional disability, compensation may not be granted for loss of future prospects.

7. In the case of Rahul Sharma v/s. National Insurance Company Ltd. [AIR 2021 SC 2255], the Hon'ble Apex Court after referring to judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. v/s. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] addressed the issue to grant compensation for loss of future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v/s. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para 10, it is held as under :-
"10.

This Court in a Five Judge Bench decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680, clearly held that in case the deceased is selfemployed and below the age of 40, 40% addition would be made to their income as future prospects.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the deceased was selfemployed and was 37 years old, therefore, warranting the addition of 40% towards future prospects.

Moreover, Pranay Sethi (supra), affirming the ratio in Sarla Verma (supra), held that the deduction towards personal and living expenses for a person such as the deceased who was married with two dependents, to be one- third (1/3 rd).
Since the High Court in the impugned judgment deducted NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined 50% the same merits interference by this Court."

8. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arun Kumar Agrawal Versus National Insurance Company [2010 (9) SCC 218], in para 51 and 52 has held as under :-

3 "51.

entities.text: Arun Kumar Agrawal Versus National Insurance Company [2010 (9) SCC 218]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In India the Courts have recognised that the contribution made by the wife to the house is invaluable and cannot be computed in terms of money.
The gratuitous services rendered by wife with true love and affection to the children and her husband and managing the household affairs cannot be equated with the services rendered by others.
A wife/ mother does not work by the clock.
She is in the constant attendance of the family throughout the day and night unless she is employed and is required to attend the employer's work for particular hours.

She takes care of all the requirements of husband and children including cooking of food, washing of clothes,
etc.
She teaches small children and provides invaluable guidance to them for their future life.

A housekeeper or maidservant can do the household work, such as cooking food, washing clothes and utensils, keeping the house clean etc., but she can never be a substitute for a wife/mother who renders selfless service to her husband and children.
52. It is not possible to quantify any amount in lieu of the services rendered by the wife/mother to the family i.e. husband and children.
However, for the purpose of award of compensation to the dependents, some pecuniary estimate has to be made of the services of housewife/mother.

In that context, the term `services' is required to be given a broad meaning and must be construed by taking into account the loss of personal care and attention given by the deceased to her children as a mother and to her husband as a wife.
They are entitled to adequate compensation in lieu of the loss of gratuitous services rendered by the deceased.

The amount payable to the dependants cannot be diminished on the ground that some close relation like a grandmother may volunteer to render some of the services to the family which the deceased was giving earlier."

9. Looking to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the submission canvassed by learned advocate Ms.Pathak that since claimant has sustained 28% functional disability, compensation for loss of future prospects may not be granted, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined cannot be accepted and is accordingly rejected.

In the present case,
the claimant was doing tailoring work as also she was home maker.
Her duty is to keep family intact 24 / 7 around the year.
Such contribution to the family cannot be equated with value of money, yet for the purpose of deciding just and fair compensation, Tribunal is required to take one figure as base figure.
Considering time period of road accident, rate of minimum wages of Rs.4660/- per month is required to be adopted.
Therefore, income of the claimant is taken as Rs.4660/- per month instead of Rs.2500/- per month.
Learned Tribunal has granted compensation under other heads in accordance with law and also applied multiplier rightly.

But so far as compensation under pain,
shock and suffering is concerned, learned Tribunal did not notice that claimant has to undergo surgery for bone grafting in both fracture and also needs surgery for removal of implants in fractures.

Looking to the facts of the case, I find fit to grant Rs.40,000/- instead of Rs.20,000/-
towards pain, shock and suffering.
10. Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.

Particulars  Dilshadbanu W/O Mohamedshafi ... vs Sureshbhai Lalbhai Nanavati on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104320257/
4  Loss of future income Rs.4660/- per month + 
 40% prospective rise = Rs.6524/- x 12 and considering 28% disability, the total amount would be Rs.21,921/- per year and applying 17 multiplier, total amount would be Rs.3,72,657/-
 
 C/FA/787/2013 ORDER DATED:
 
 Actual loss of income (Rs.4660/- x 3) 
 Medical expenses   Special diet, transportation and attendant   charges.
 Mental pain, shock and suffering   Total... 
 Less : Amount which is already awarded   Additional amount which is awarded  11.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant is entitled to get the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,56,337/-
with 8% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
12. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
12.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.2,56,337/- with 8% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition till its realization before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

12.2 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimant, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.

While making the payment, the Tribunal shall de the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
12.4 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
